The domain decomposition method decomposes a photomask layout into constituent single-opening masks using the linearity of the Kirchhoff-Fresnel diffraction integral.
Two rigorous 2D electromagnetic simulations in cross-sectional planes replace computationally expensive 3D simulations.
Compact equivalent source models are constructed to minimize errors in the diffraction spectrum passing through the projection system.
Normalized mean square error of the near scattered field is typically less than 1% compared to full rigorous simulations.
Speed-up factors exceeding 400 times are achieved in total simulation time relative to rigorous 3D mask models.
The method accounts for the chromium absorption layer transmission by subtracting its effect multiple times during decomposition.
Mk-mask models are modified k-mask models with adjusted transmission functions that closely match rigorous r-mask diffraction spectra.
The method accurately captures the intensity imbalance effect in alternating phase-shifting masks that k-mask models fail to represent.
Through-the-lens (TTL) diffraction orders are the subset of diffraction orders collected by the projection system's numerical aperture.
The finite difference time-domain solver TEMPEST is used for rigorous electromagnetic field simulations.
The SPLAT simulator is used for aerial image formation based on mask scattering models.
The domain decomposition method has been extended to include energy cross-coupling (crosstalk) between neighboring apertures in alt PSMs.
The method supports arbitrary polygonal mask openings beyond rectangular shapes through further developments.
Off-axis illumination is modeled by adjusting the numerical aperture acceptance cone and partial coherence factors.
The method enables rapid and accurate simulation critical for model-based OPC and mask defect evaluation.
The electromagnetic near field below the mask is represented by six field components (Ex, Ey, Ez, Hx, Hy, Hz) in the rigorous model.
The k-mask model assumes a piecewise constant complex mask transmission function, which is insufficient for advanced photomasks.
The domain decomposition method was validated on a 400 nm 1:1 line/space alt PSM pattern with 80 nm thick chromium absorption layer.
The method achieves better than 0.5% accuracy in near-field scattered field for shallow-trench alt PSMs.
The method's decomposition approach is analogous to superposition of electromagnetic fields from individual mask openings.
